title: Using a language reference
recap: A language reference is organized for precise lookup: headers, signatures, version availability, preconditions, return values, and invalidation or lifetime notes matter more than a quick example alone.
std::clamp assumes ordered bounds and returns a reference to one of its arguments. This wrapper normalizes the bounds and returns an int by value, so no reference to a local parameter escapes.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Use the standard-library reference linked in lesson.md to implement boundedTemperature(reading,low,high). If low > high, swap the bounds first. Then return reading clamped to the inclusive interval. Practice finding std::clamp requirements, return type, and header rather than copying an unrelated example. All values are ints.
hints: Read the precondition on std::clamp before using it.
Normalize reversed bounds with a temporary or std::swap.
Return an int value rather than storing a reference to a temporary result.
